business.title: OpenAI launches Korea cyber action plan with expanded AI security access
business.description: MLex Summary: OpenAI on Wednesday said it is expanding the access of South Korean government agencies, public institutions and companies to its advanced AI cyber-defense capabilities under a new "Korea Cyber Action Plan." The initiative will broaden South Korean participation in OpenAI’s Trusted Access for Cyber, or TAC, program, which provides vetted entities with access to advanced cybersecurity-focused AI models, following recent demonstrations and discussions with ministries and public agencies including the Korea Internet & Security Agency and the Ministry of Science and ICT. OpenAI said the plan would also extend TAC access to major companies in critical South Korean industries while widening cooperation in areas including climate-disaster response, public-sector finance and AI startup support.

ai.title: Dropbox founder Drew Houston steps down.
ai.description:
Steve Jobs famously told Houston his startup was “a feature, not a product” when trying to acquire it back in 2009. Houston turned down the nine-figure buyout offer and Apple went on to launch iCloud. Houston, now 43 and worth about $2 billion, leaves behind a service used by millions worldwide. He now wants to do something entrepreneurial with — you guessed it — AI.
[Link: Dropbox CEO Drew Houston to step down after 19 years at helm of cloud storage pioneer | https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/26/dropbox-ceo-drew-houston-ashraf-alkarmi.html | CNBC]

ai.title: Asian shares are mostly higher, tracking Wall Street's fresh records, and oil prices fall
ai.description: Asian shares are mostly higher and oil prices have fallen after the U.S. stock market rose to records. South Korea's Kospi jumped more than 2% and Taiwan's benchmark also surged as the boom in artificial intelligence drove heavy buying of computer chipmakers and other technology companies. On Tuesday, the S&P 500 climbed 0.6% after trading resumed following Monday’s holiday, setting another all-time high. The Nasdaq composite rallied 1.2% to its own record, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average dipped 0.2% from its all-time high. Micron Technology led the way, and its stock has more than tripled so far this year. Treasury yields eased.
